newsitem.title: UK: IFC Emerging market equity, debt indices ease.
newsitem.headline: IFC Emerging market equity, debt indices ease.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, fell 0.7 percent to 334.88 by midsession on Thursday.
Latin America lost 1.3 percent day-on-day to 637.99, Asia was down 0.4 percent at 268.67, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were down 0.5 percent at 163.52.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was down 0.84 percent day-on-day at 180.30 at 1300 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was down 0.66 percent at 533.677, calculated after the close of trade on Wednesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, fell 0.24 percent to 127.28 by the start of trade on Thursday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was down 0.37 percent at 106.79, Asia fell 0.09 to 133.10 and East Europe was down 0.46 at 159.58.
